output.brief: Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is inside the service's normal range. Over the previous 26 weeks it averaged 0.354%, and the upper edge of the normal band is 0.482%. Three earlier weeks were higher (0.51%, 0.47%, 0.45%), and investigating them found nothing. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). Under your own policy this week is noted at ops review and no action is taken. The dashboard counts match raw logs, so this is not a counting artefact. The finding that new pods error at almost twice the rate of old ones is a rollout warm-up effect. It appears in every recent rollout, including a config-only redeploy, and it accounts for only 10–20 extra errors. It doesn't show a fault in v4.18. Customer bookings were flat and there were no complaints. I would not roll back, and I would not mute alerting, since that removes the protection that would catch a real problem. I'd keep the replica fallback hosts in place and apply the standard check to next week. I'm fairly confident, but I did not rule out the replica move or partner-sync month-end traffic as small contributors. If next week's rate is above the band, investigate then.
output.methodChoice: Collected X11 (normal band) and X6 (rollout warm-up baseline) as the most discriminating items.
